results.intro: In *Williams v. Emergency Groups' Office*, 2012 WL 1032700 (2012), the Court of Appeal affirmed, in an unpublished decision, the trial court's denial of class certification under the Rosenthal Act for alleged infirmities in the collection of medical bills. The Court of Appeal found, in part, that the Plaintiffs' class definition was too broad because it necessarily would have included non-delinquent accounts, that are not subject to the Rosenthal Act.

In *McQueen v. American Exp. Centurion Bank*, 2012 WL 5301075 (N.D.Cal. 2012), Judge James dismissed a Plaintiff's FDCPA claim on a Rule 12(b)(6) motion because the defendant was a creditor, exempt from the FDCPA.

In *Callahan v. Equifax Information Services LLC,* 2013 WL 5503949 (N.D.Cal. 2013), Judge Alsup found that Plaintiff could state a FCRA claim in an SSN-swap situation.

results.intro: In *Chaiwong v. Hanlees Fremont, Inc.,* 2017 WL 3838106 (N.D. Cal. Sept. 1, 2017), Judge Gilliam dismissed a Rosenthal Act/UCL claim filed against an automobile lender by a consumer and the dealer to whom the customer traded in their vehicle.

In *Fishman v. Tiger Natural Gas, Inc.,* 2018 WL 1242076, at *2--3 (N.D.Cal., 2018), Judge Alsup allowed a call-recording class action to proceed. Tiger argues that plaintiffs' allegations regarding the sales calls --- namely that (1) the parties discussed plaintiffs' PG&E account information, (2) the calls were not made in a public setting, and (3) many other telemarketers disclose that calls are recorded --- are insufficient to allege an objectively reasonable expectation of confidentiality.
In Keifer v. Hosopo Corp., No.: 3:18-cv-1353-CAB-(KSC), 2018 WL 5295011 (S.D. Cal. Oct. 25, 2018), the Court found that a TCPA Plaintiff adequately pleaded an ATDS after Marks.
In Moser v. Health Ins. Innovations, Inc., No. 17-cv-1127-WQH-KSC, 2019 U.S. Dist. LEXIS 132790 (S.D. Cal. Aug. 2, 2019), Judge Hayes certified a TCPA class.

In Walker v. Westlake Fin. Servs., No. 19 C 6921, 2020 U.S. Dist. LEXIS 105794 (N.D. Ill. June 17, 2020), Judge Kendall permitted an FDCPA/TCPA defendant to file a counter-claim on the debt back against the Plaintiff.

In Pearson v. April Healthcare Grp., 2021 U.S.Dist.LEXIS 90010 (S.D.Cal. 2021), Judge Hayes granted summary judgment to a debt collector attempting to collect a medical debt despite the availability of medical insurance.

In Barton v. Serve All Help All Inc., No. 3:21-cv-5338 RJB, 2022 U.S. Dist. LEXIS 161487, at *8 (W.D. Wash. Sep. 7, 2022), Judge Bryan denied summary judgment all around, but also denied a TCPA defendant's jurisdictional motion.

analysis_note: 3/20 samples had court_id="fcc" (a load_corpus.py court-detection false positive — those posts mention FCC somewhere but are not FCC proceedings; "fcc" is not a valid CourtListener court code, so those 3 were guaranteed misses). Excluding them: 4/17 = 23.5% on real court queries. Separately, a live sweep of TODAY's published opinions (non-backtest, see pipeline/ingest/sweep.py test run) found 4/4 recent 9th Cir. TCPA opinions with full text, unauthenticated. The gap is specific to RECAP/unpublished DISTRICT COURT orders (exactly what 74% of Scott's historical WL-cited posts are) as unauthenticated RECAP search is much weaker than the CourtListener opinion search. This backtest is also a pessimistic proxy: it is asking whether we can find OLD (2008-2022) cases years later, not whether we can catch NEW cases the day they are decided (which RECAP webhook alerts are built for, and which a token substantially improves). Re-run with COURTLISTENER_TOKEN set once Scott/Trevor create an account to get the number that actually governs go-live — this run is the conservative unauthenticated floor.
